records.name: Elfreth's Alley Association, Inc
records.summary: Keeps Elfreth's Alley and its history in view. The association runs a small museum in two of the Alley's houses, leads guided tours, and holds events such as a fall makers market and a December holiday event.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers greet visitors and share Alley history, help run events like the makers market and Deck the Alley, or do project work such as garden upkeep, building care, and archives. Anyone can visit the museum or join a guided tour.

schedule.text: Museum open Friday to Sunday, noon to 4 pm. Guided tours Saturday and Sunday at 2:30 pm. Volunteers can come weekly, monthly, or only for major events.

cost.text: Museum: $3 for adults and $2 for children 7 to 12. Guided tour: $10 for adults and $5 for children 7 to 12, museum included.

first_step.how: Fill out the volunteer interest form on the Volunteer with Us page, or visit the museum on a Friday to Sunday afternoon.
first_step.basis: The volunteer page says no history background is needed, training is provided, and a packet of common questions is given to new people.

records.notes: Lead address reads 126 Elfreths Aly; the site says the museum is at 124 and 126. The newest blog posts are from 2025, so the 2026 activity rests on the October to December 2026 event listings. The old /volunteer link returns 404; the live page is /volunteer-with-us. Volunteer training dates are not yet posted.

records.name: Fever Dream Repertory
records.summary: Theater company that stages its own productions in Philadelphia and sells tickets to them. Its public roles are attending shows, auditioning for paid roles, and donating.
records.notes: No classes, volunteer, membership or community program found. Auditions are by appointment for paid, non-union roles, and the August 2026 call for The Lyons has passed; the group hires actors, which is closer to a job than to joining a group. The Lyons runs Nov 6 to 15, 2026 at Skinner Studio. Re-check if they open classes, volunteering or a community program. The batch address is a residential apartment unit, so it is not recorded.

records.name: Historic Gloria Dei Preservation Corporation (Preserve Old Swedes)
records.summary: Looks after Gloria Dei (Old Swedes') Church as a historic site. It hosts history talks and concerts, runs guided tours, and calls on volunteers for service days on the grounds.
records.what_you_do: Attend a Great Talk or a concert, take a guided tour, or join a community service day to help care for the church and grounds. A volunteer link on the website is the way to offer help.

schedule.text: Great Talks and concerts are on set dates. Calendar entries include a talk on Sept 29, 2026, a talk on Oct 8, 2026, and a concert on Oct 25, 2026 at 3 pm. Service days are announced on the website.

cost.text: Talks listed at $12 to $15. Concert listed at $15 to $30. Research requests are a $40 flat fee for up to 60 minutes.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket to the Oct 25, 2026 concert or to a future Great Talk, or use the volunteer link on preserveoldswedes.org to sign up for a service day.
first_step.basis: Talks and concerts are open to ticket buyers and volunteering is offered, but the site does not say how newcomers are brought into service days.

records.notes: The events page says it lists 35 events but only 3 were visible in the capture, so more dates may exist. The church street address is not shown on the site; the address comes from the Cultural Fund and IRS lead data. The volunteer form and tour booking details were not opened.

records.name: Independence Historical Trust
records.summary: Philanthropic partner to Independence National Historical Park. It raises money for restoration and public projects, runs public talks, movie nights and tours, and uses volunteers for tours and events.
records.what_you_do: Lead free summer Twilight Tours, help staff events such as the Pops on Independence concert and the annual meeting, or help in the office. The public can attend talks, movie nights, Halloween events and tours.

schedule.text: Twilight Tours run daily in the summer. Public events are listed by date on the events page, including a speaker series, Movies on the Mall, and Halloween events in October and November.

cost.text: The volunteer page says the summer tours are free for visitors and locals. Other event prices are not listed.

first_step.how: Fill out the volunteer form on the Volunteering page, or call 215-861-4971 or email attn@inht.org to ask about tour guide or event roles.
first_step.basis: The Trust says it will email interested volunteers when openings come up, but it does not say who can volunteer or what training is given.

records.notes: Event dates on the events page are listed without years, and the year 2026 was not confirmed on the page, so the status is probably_active rather than active. Twilight Tours, the speaker series and Movies on the Mall are listed; no street address for events is shown. The Trust says the summer tour roles are seasonal.

records.name: Indigenous Peoples' Day Philly Inc
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit working to make Indigenous Peoples' Day a permanent city holiday. It holds a public celebration each October and runs Indigenous-led programs and community meetings.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer for the Oct 12, 2026 celebration, attend community meetings for the holiday campaign, sign the petition, or join, donate, or subscribe through the website.

schedule.text: Public celebration on Monday, Oct 12, 2026 at Shackamaxon (Penn Treaty) Park. The holiday is the second Monday of October each year. Campaign community meetings are announced on the website.

cost.text: Admission to the celebration is not stated. The group is seeking sponsors for the 2026 event.

first_step.how: Go to the Oct 12, 2026 celebration at Shackamaxon (Penn Treaty) Park, or send a volunteer question through the contact form on ipdphilly.org.
first_step.basis: The event is open to anyone and volunteer positions are posted, but the site gives no welcome steps for first-time volunteers.

records.notes: The site gives a founding date of 2017-10-12. Posting dates for the event calls and media kit are not shown. The phone line is a voicemail. The mailing address is a PMB box, so it is not recorded as a location.

records.name: Inis Nua Theatre Company
records.summary: Theater company that stages modern plays by writers from Ireland and Britain. Its public roles are buying season tickets, attending shows, and donating.
records.notes: No classes, volunteer roles, usher program, membership or community program found. The Reading Series is listed for Nov 17, 2026, Mar 22, 2027 and June 14, 2027, but its admission terms are not stated, so it cannot be treated as an open public program. Re-check if the Reading Series is free and open to anyone, or if volunteer or usher roles appear. Jobs and Submissions is for artists.

records.name: Irish Heritage Theatre
records.summary: Theater company that produces Irish and Irish American plays. Its public role is attending productions, plus a newsletter sign-up.
records.notes: No classes, volunteer, usher, audition, membership or community program listed. The newest dated item is a 2023-02-20 scholarship news post; the 2026 season page has no dates. The site's copyright year is not evidence. If they open classes, volunteering or a community program, re-check.

records.name: Jewish Chorale of Greater Philadelphia (Nashirah)
records.summary: A nonprofit choir that sings the full range of Jewish choral music for audiences in the region. Singers join through an audition, and the choir performs concerts through its season.
records.what_you_do: Audition to sing in the choir, or attend one of its concerts. Auditions for the 2026 to 2027 season are open to prospective members.

schedule.text: Concerts through the 2026 to 2027 season. Auditions are by appointment, in person or online.

cost.text: Audition and membership costs are not shown on the site.

first_step.how: Email manager@nashirah.org to book an audition for the 2026 to 2027 season, in person or online. Arrive at least 15 minutes early; sight-reading, tonal memory, rhythm, vocal range and tone are checked.
first_step.basis: Joining requires an audition booked by appointment, and the site does not describe a beginner route or who may audition.

records.notes: The old domain nashirah.org redirects (301) to nashirahphila.wordpress.com, which is the site used here. The group calls itself Nashirah. The site shows a 2026 to 2027 season and an audition poster but no posting dates, so status is probably_active. The mailing address is a P.O. box and is not recorded as a location. The audition page does not say whether anyone may audition.

records.name: Koresh Dance Company
records.summary: Dance company based at Rittenhouse Square that also runs a studio with adult and children's classes. Its public work includes performances, outreach, and a school.
records.what_you_do: Take an adult drop-in dance class at the studio, such as ballet, contemporary modern, jazz, musical theater, or East African contemporary. Children can join the Fall Session, and the public can attend the Artist Showcase or the Oct 24 masquerade.

schedule.text: Adult drop-in classes Monday to Saturday, mostly 6 to 9 pm on weekdays and late morning to early afternoon on Saturdays. Children's Fall Session with late registration open. Artist Showcase ticket sales Oct 10 and 11, 2026.

cost.text: Adult drop-in $20 general or $19 student or professional. Class cards of 10 classes from $180 to $190. First-time visitors can take 3 classes for $45.

first_step.how: Book a first-time class through the online class schedule (online pre-registration is encouraged), or call 215-751-0959. Ask about the 3 classes for $45 first-timer offer.
first_step.basis: The site lists a first-timer offer and beginner-level classes, and adult drop-in classes need no membership.

records.notes: Adult classes are for ages 13 and up. The Children's Fall Session has no ages, days or prices on the site. Class styles are not a vocabulary tag, so the interest is dance_company. The Oct 24 masquerade is listed as 8 pm with no year on the page; it sits with the 2026 showcase.

records.name: Lantern Theater Company
records.summary: Theater company that stages plays in Philadelphia and sells season subscriptions and tickets. Its education programs are for schools.
records.notes: Public roles are subscriptions, tickets, donations and the Email Club sign-up. The education page lists student matinees, classroom residencies and teacher training, all for schools or teachers only. No volunteer, usher, class, membership or public community program found. Re-check if they open volunteer or usher roles.

records.name: Liberty City Arts
records.summary: An artist-run opera group in Philadelphia. The homepage says it offers free vocal training and performance chances for Philadelphia-rooted artists, and it puts on public shows and cabarets.
records.what_you_do: Attend a public opera or cabaret event, or ask about free vocal training and performance chances for Philadelphia artists through the Contact Us page.

schedule.text: September 2026 shows: Never Land (Sept 10 and 12) and My Place of Clear Water (Sept 15 and 22). No vocal training schedule is published.

cost.text: Ticket prices are not shown on the upcoming events page. The site mentions complimentary artist tickets for artists.

first_step.how: Ask about free vocal training or performance chances through the Contact Us page at libertycityarts.org, or buy a ticket to the next event on the Upcoming Events page.
first_step.basis: Training is described as free, but the site gives no schedule, eligibility rules or sign-up steps, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: The homepage mentions free vocal training, but no training schedule, eligibility rule or sign-up route was found on the pages read. The upcoming events page lists only September 2026 dates, so check again for newer events. The Get Involved page does not describe free training, volunteering or membership.

records.name: Lyra Society
records.summary: A harp nonprofit that teaches harp and helps students with college applications at partner Philadelphia public schools, at no cost to them. Adults can volunteer on its committees and attend public concerts and benefits.
records.what_you_do: Join a volunteer committee (college guidance, development and marketing, events, finance, technology and website, or the Young Friends group for ages 21 to 65), or attend a public concert or benefit. Students at partner schools take part through the Glissando Program.

schedule.text: Public concerts, showcases and benefits are listed through the year, most recently a June 3, 2026 golf benefit at Union League Golf Club at Torresdale. Committee meeting times are not stated.

cost.text: Glissando services are free to students at partner schools. Public event prices are not shown on the events page.

first_step.how: Email info@LyraSociety.org with your resume or LinkedIn profile and the committee you want to join, or attend a public event listed on the events page.
first_step.basis: Volunteering asks for a resume and a committee choice, so the way in is a short application rather than a casual sign-up.

records.notes: The Glissando Program serves students in six Philadelphia and Bronx schools, so the general public cannot join it directly. Most events listed are invite-only or for students; the public ones include the March 2026 showcase, the March 2026 gala and the June 2026 golf benefit. The Young Friends committee is for ages 21 to 65. Batch P.O. box is not recorded as a location.

records.name: MacGuffin Theatre & Film Company
records.summary: A nonprofit theater group that teaches acting classes and camps for children and teens. It also runs troupes for improv, cabaret, comedy and acting, and holds auditions for its shows.
records.what_you_do: Take an acting class in the fall, winter or spring term, sign a child up for a youth camp or after-school class, or join a troupe such as improv, cabaret or comedy. Auditions are held for productions.

schedule.text: Classes run in the Fall 2026, Winter 2027 and Spring 2027 terms, with after-school programs and camps in 2026. Exact class days and times are on the class pages.

cost.text: Class and camp prices are not on the summary page. The group offers scholarships.

first_step.how: Look at the Fall 2026 and Winter 2027 classes on the website and sign up for one, or email info@macguffintf.com to ask about the next term and scholarships.
first_step.basis: Classes, camps and auditions are open to the public with a clear way to sign up, but the site does not say that beginners are specifically welcome.

records.notes: Age groups listed are youth 7 to 10 and middlers and teens 11 to 17; adult class ages are not stated. The last_sign_of_life month is the start of the Fall 2026 term, because the page shows no posting date. Photos and videos from classes and shows may be used for promotion, and participants can opt out. The artistic director is named on the site as John Rea.

records.name: Mexican Cultural Center
records.summary: A nonprofit that shares Mexican heritage with Philadelphians through festivals, Day of the Dead events, programs and workshops. Its events are open to everyone, and volunteers can sign up through a form.
records.what_you_do: Attend a public festival or Day of the Dead event, join as a member, or fill out the volunteer form to help at events.

schedule.text: Events through the year. Mexican Independence Day Festival on Sept 13, 2026, 2 to 7 pm at RiverRink Summerfest. Day of the Dead at the Penn Museum on Oct 24, 2026, 1 to 4 pm.

cost.text: The Mexican Independence Day Festival is listed as free. Other event prices are not shown; membership, donations and sponsorships are offered.

first_step.how: Fill out the volunteer form on the website, or attend the Day of the Dead event at the Penn Museum on Oct 24, 2026 from 1 to 4 pm.
first_step.basis: Events are open to the public and the volunteer form is a clear way in, but the site describes no beginner or newcomer route.

records.notes: Events are open to everyone, not limited to one heritage, so no heritage audience tag is set. The Contact Us page holds the group's email form; the site shows the email only as a placeholder. The membership, volunteer and contribution pages linked from the homepage were not opened.

records.name: Mutya Philippine Dance Company, Inc
records.summary: Filipino dance and music company that performs and can be booked for events. Its public role is booking a performance or giving a donation.
records.notes: No public classes, auditions, volunteer roles or open membership found. The For Members page returned HTTP 401 (members only), and the Alumni Registration page is for past dancers. The only public way in is requesting a performance, which is booking rather than joining. The company's mission mentions teaching dance, so re-check if classes or open auditions appear. The newest dated item is the 2025 35th anniversary (year only).

records.name: Orchestra 2001, Inc.
records.summary: An ensemble that plays 20th and 21st century music. Its community work includes free and pay-what-you-wish pop-up concerts at markets and public events.
records.what_you_do: Go to a free pop-up concert or a public concert, sign up for e-news, or ask about volunteering, an internship, or the board through the Support page.

schedule.text: Pop-up and public concerts through the year. Recent dated events: Sept 24, 2026 jazz duo at Fairmount Farmers Market, and Oct 3, 2026 Firstival at Eastern State Penitentiary (free, 10 am to 2 pm, with pop-ups 11:30 am to 12:30 pm).

cost.text: Some events are free or pay-what-you-wish; others are ticketed. Prices vary by event.

first_step.how: Go to the next free pop-up concert listed on the events page, or send a volunteer or internship question through the Support page.
first_step.basis: Free public concerts need no sign-up, but the site does not describe how volunteers or interns are chosen.

records.notes: The events list includes older 2022 to 2025 items. The Playing the Markets 2025 to 2026 pop-ups are undated. No instrument tag fits the ensemble, so interests are left empty.

records.name: Performance Garage
records.summary: A dance center in a renovated former stable on Brandywine Street. It hosts classes taught by resident companies and instructors, youth and education programs, performances, and a 105-seat theater.
records.what_you_do: Take a class taught by a resident company or instructor (ballet, Bollywood, Bharatanatyam, or early childhood music), or see a performance at the center.

schedule.text: Classes are run by outside instructors and their dates and times are not on the summary page. Performances and the annual gala are held through the year; the Gala 2026 page shows no date.

cost.text: Class prices are not shown. Contact the instructor or Performance Garage for fees.

first_step.how: Open the Classes page, pick a class (ballet, Bollywood, Bharatanatyam, or early childhood music), and contact that instructor or company for dates, ages and prices.
first_step.basis: The site lists classes but gives no ages, levels, registration steps or prices, so the way in is unclear. Rehearsals are closed to the public.

records.notes: Class providers named on the classes page: Chocolate Ballerina, Alexei Borovik, Alexei Charov and Natalia Charova (ballet), Daksha Dance Troupe (Bollywood), Nardhana Academy (Bharatanatyam), and Mister John's Music (early childhood music). The founding year 2000 is the only dated item and no event is dated. The Gala 2026 page has no date or venue.

records.name: Philadelphia Arts in Education Partnership (PAEP)
records.summary: A nonprofit that brings working artists and scientists into schools and community sites for hands-on arts and STEAM lessons. Families can enroll students in its STEAM afterschool program, and artists can apply to teach.
records.what_you_do: Enroll a student in the STEAM Afterschool Program, apply on the website to become a STEAM Educator (a teaching artist or scientist role), or ask a school to become a participating organization.

schedule.text: The STEAM afterschool schedule is not shown on the site. Teaching roles are limited and filled by application.

cost.text: Program fees are not shown on the site. The group accepts donations.

first_step.how: Ask a school or site that works with PAEP to register your child for the STEAM Afterschool Program, or apply through the website to become a STEAM Educator.
first_step.basis: Afterschool registration depends on partner sites, and educator roles need an application and are limited.

records.notes: The site gives no street address or phone number. The IRS lead lists 440 N Broad St, which is not confirmed on the site, so it is not recorded. Public routes run mostly through schools and partner sites. The Sept 2026 news names a new executive director, Anjoli Santiago.

notes: All 18 batch groups have a record. Verdict counts: publish 13, not_a_group 5 (Fever Dream Repertory, Inis Nua Theatre Company, Irish Heritage Theatre, Lantern Theater Company, Mutya Philippine Dance Company). Searches used: 0 (none allowed). Fetches used: 50 of 60. Not every page was checked: the Gloria Dei, IHT and Liberty City Arts event pages showed partial lists. The Elfreth's old /volunteer link is a 404; the live page is /volunteer-with-us. Lead addresses were handled as follows: Fever Dream's batch address is a residential apartment unit and is not recorded; PAEP's lead address (440 N Broad St) is not on its site and is not recorded; Gloria Dei's church address comes from the lead data only and is flagged in its record. Statuses rest on dated items found on the group's own pages; several records use the month of a listed 2026 event as last_sign_of_life because the page gives no posting date. No budget was exhausted.
